# Brand Discovery

Curated by Skill Harbor: a brand-identity interview skill that runs a structured, adaptive, multi-session interview and turns implicit founder knowledge into a master brandbook. Eight modules run in order (purpose, positioning, audience and niche, personality and archetype, voice and tone, narrative, founder tension, final synthesis), using laddering, 5 Whys, and projective techniques (brand obituary, competitive contrast) to push past surface answers. The interview discipline is strict: one question at a time, paraphrase plus one deepening probe after each answer, thin answers get challenged with a request for a concrete example, and every module ends with a Raw section (verbatim quotes) plus a Synthesis section (interpretation, candidate formulations, open questions). Progress persists to disk (module files plus a state.json checkpoint), so a later session resumes exactly where the last one stopped, and multi-founder mode interviews each stakeholder separately before a reconciliation pass to avoid anchoring bias. The deliverable is 90_SYNTHESIS.md: a master brandbook for briefing designers, writers, and collaborators. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: this is designed for multiple sessions over days or weeks, rushing it in one sitting produces shallow output; it needs an agent that can write files for the persistence to work; it makes implicit knowledge explicit, which can surface uncomfortable...
